texts.preamble: Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Digitally signed by Shambulingayya Shambulingayya Gadagayya Gadagayya Mudimath Mudimath Date: 2024.05.30 15:27:28 +0530 Kabc020166182019 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore. (Scch-9) Dated This The 29th Day Of May, 2024 Present: SRI.Shambhulingayya Mudimath.B.Com., Ll.B (Spl) Judge Scj, Acmm & Mact , Bengaluru. Mvc No.3841/2019 Petitioner: Sri.Ramanna, S/o.Muligiriyappa, Aged about 45 years, Since the petitioner is mentally disorder Rep. by his wife Smt.Chandramma, Aged about 38 years, R/at Kuppuru, Bugudanahalli Post Tumkur Taluk & Dist. (By Sri. Jagadeesha - Adv.) V/s. Respondents: The Managing Director, Ksrtc Depot, Bangalore Central office, K.H.Road, Shanthinagar, (Scch-9) 2 MVC.No.3841/2019 Bangalore - 560027. (Rc Owner of Ksrtc Bus Bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010) (By Sri.MSB - Adv.) 2) Chandraiah.D., S/o.Dasappa, Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/ 1 Kuppuru, Bugudanahalli Post, Bellavi Hobli, Tumkur District. (Rc Owner of Tvs Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EM-122) (By Sri.RMR - Adv.) Judgment
texts.facts: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under: On 27-04-2019 at about 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on two wheeler bearing No.KA-06-EM-122 on Old NH-4, Sira Road, when he reached (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.3841/2019 Opposite to Maruthi Rice Mill, near Sridevi Hostel, Lingapura, Tumkur. At that time, the driver of KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010 came in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle. Due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over his body. Immediately he was shifted to Shridevi Institute of Medical Science and Research Hospital, Sira, wherein X-rays were taken which revealed fracture injuries and then referred to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 28.04.2019 to 30.04.2019 and then referred to Victora Hospital, wherein also he took treatment as inpatient from 01.05.2019 to 07.05.2019 and after necessary treatment he was discharged with an advise to take followup treatment. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3841/2019 The petitioner has lost his earning capacity and cannot do his normal work prior to the accident. The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010. The jurisdictional Police have registered a Criminal Case against the driver of KSRTC Bus in Cr.No.109/2019 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC. After investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of KSRTC Bus. The respondent being RC Owner and Insurer of the KSRTC Bus is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation. 3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/ 2 This respondent has denied the contents of claim (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3841/2019 petition specifically and categorically. It has contended that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., the rider of TVS Excel bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EM-122 was solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident. The owner and insurer of Motor Cycle are necessary parties. The driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1010 was no way responsible for the alleged accident, consequently respondent is not a necessary party to the proceedings. It has specifically denied the manner of accident, the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. It has also denied the injuries sustained, treatment taken and expenses incurred towards medicine. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. With this ground it has prayed to dismiss the petition. The 2nd respondent subsequently added on the basis of written statement filed by 1st respondent with regard to non joinder of necessary party. (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.3841/2019 The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is as under: This respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically. This respondent has admitted the petition averments with regard to accident and treatment taken by the petitioner. This respondent has also admitted he was the rider of the motor cycle bearing Regn No.KA-06-EM-122 as on the date of accident. In order to prove his case, the Dr.Shailesh.A.V. Rao was examined as PW.1 and got marked document at Ex.P1 to Ex.P3. Smt.Chandramma wife of petitioner was examined as PW2 and document at Ex.P4 to 17 were got exhibited. In order to prove the case, the wife of petitioner herself examined as PW.2 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
texts.arguments: This respondent further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence prayed for rejecting the petition. This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others). 14. At the time of arguments the learned counsel for 1st respondent has vehemently argued and submitted that there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle and it was caused on the sole negligence of rider of motor cycle. Hence petition is liable to be dismiss. In this regard he relied upon the judgments reported in 1) (2005) 6 SCC 172 (National Ins.CoLtd., Premabai Patel 7 Ors,), 2) (2014) 13 SCC 254 (Lachoo Ram & Others - Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/ 5 (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.3841/2019 V/s- Himachal Road Transport Corporation), 3) MFA 2829/2009 (MV) (Manju V/s Mathue.K.P & Ors.) and 4) MFA.2921/2012 (Smt.Vijayalakshmi.K.N., & others V/s Karnataka State Road Transport) with due respect to these judgments, the facts and circumstances of these judgments are different from the present case on hand, hence not applicable to present case on hand. The argument advanced by the learned counsel for 1 st respondent holds no water. Therefore, the documents relied by petitioner and oral evidence of PW2 clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010. Now it can safely be concluded, that the injuries were caused to the petitioner due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the KSRTC Bus. The petitioner contended that he took treatment at hospital and produced medical bills marked at Ex.P14 for Rs.13,168/-. Hence the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,168/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses. 18. At the time of argument the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has vehemently argued and submitted that there is a contributory negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle, he further submitted that at the time of accident there were 3 persons were riding in the motor cycle and there was a every chance of non control of the motor cycle by the rider while triple riding. Therefore the (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.3841/2019 rider of the motor cycle has also contributed in causing the accident. In this regard he relied upon judgments reported in ILR 2003 KAR 409 (P.Varalakshmi Reddy & Ors. V/s The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation) and MFA 4193/2007 c/w 10454/07 (P.Anki Reddy & another V/s The Oriental Insurance & Ors. V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., & Ors.). In this regard I would like to rely upon the judgments reported in 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others), wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then contributory negligence to be considered and compensation should be apportioned on the apportionment of negligence. 2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn) Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a negligence and contributory negligence be considered while awarding the compensation in accident case. 3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co.., Ltd., V/s (SCCH-9) 25 MVC.No.3841/2019 Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of triple riding there is a contributory negligence and liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance companies. 4) The unreported judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.5314/2009 (MV) between H.B. Hemakeshwarappa V/s Abdul Roop Khan observed that-in a motor cycle if three persons were riding it is a negligent on the part of rider of the motor cycle. Hence, not entitled for any compensation against the insurer. 19. The ratio laid down in the above cited judgments reveals that when there was riding of motor cycle more than seating capacity then it is to be considered as contributory negligence and Tribunal Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/ 9 has to fix some percentage of liability on insurer of offending vehicle and some percentage of liability on owner of injured vehicle fastening contributory negligence. The one of the above cited judgment Managing Director, Tamil (SCCH-9) 26 MVC.No.3841/2019 Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Division)Limited Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam And othres where in Hon'ble Madras High Court held in detail at para No.10, 11 and 12 as under:- " 10. We are concerned as to whether such action of the individuals is permissible under law.
